This is one axial slice of a T2-weighted fat-suppressed MRI (radiological convention: patient right on image left, anterior at top). It contains a fibrous soft-tissue tumor. Typical appearance: Fibrous tumor (desmoid fibromatosis or undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma): a soft-tissue mass roughly isointense to muscle on T1 and of intermediate-to-high, heterogeneous signal on fat-suppressed T2, where dense collagen forms dark bands. Desmoids have infiltrative margins and often a linear tail along a fascial plane; myxoid or necrotic parts of a sarcoma are brighter on T2.

The left panel is the clean image; the right panel shows numbered marks. Choose the ONE mark that lies inside the tumor, as close to its centre as possible. End your reply with a final line exactly: ANSWER: <mark number>

The marks near this region are 483 (1100, 121), 481 (1220, 191), 480 (1230, 236), 479 (1215, 311) and 478 (1185, 331).

- Mark 480 sits at the right edge of the dark mass, around x=1230. The mass extends to roughly x=1210 at y=236, so 480 is probably just outside it.
- Mark 478 at (1185, 331) is near the lower-right edge. The mass boundary there runs around x=1180 at y=320, so it is borderline.
- Mark 483 at (1100, 121) lies in the upper region, which looks like bowel or other structures rather than the mass.
